See it in action

Real moments, made easier.

Here’s what life actually looks like when your home has a system behind it.

Every morning

Your day, already oriented.

Flow opens with a greeting, your day’s theme, and one question: how’s today feeling? Smooth, Busy, or Survival — the app meets you where you are and adjusts accordingly.

“Hard day? Tap Survival — it’s okay.” That’s not a feature. That’s a philosophy.

Whenever it’s building up

Exhale. Clear your mind — then let it go.

Everything nagging at you goes here. Compass reads your captures and notices patterns before you do — so nothing stays lost in your head.

“Compass noticed: batch similar errands into a single weekly review.”

Every week

The whole week’s meals, in one place.

Meals planned by day, pulled from your Meal Bank, with notes for the ones that matter. Everyone sees the same plan — no more “what’s for dinner?”

“End of school celebration!” — the little notes that make a meal plan feel like a family plan.

Whenever the mood strikes

A place for everything your family is thinking about.

Cove holds your household’s lists, notes, and ideas — baby’s first 100 foods, house projects, summer bucket lists, books to read. Start from a template or build your own.

No rigid structure. Just your family’s life, organized the way you actually think.

Ripples

The things you don’t want to forget.

Most of running a household is remembering what has to happen. Ripples is for remembering what did. The first smile. The funny word your three-year-old invented. The tradition only your family does.

These moments come fast and fade faster — Ripples lets you catch them in seconds, right when they happen, kept safe in the same place your household already lives.

Because the lists were never the point. This was the point.

Our story

Built by a parent who was carrying too much.

Two days before a family vacation, I realized our dog’s vaccines were overdue. The reminder lived nowhere — except my head. That same year, I discovered that my nursing license had lapsed. I’m a nurse. Keeping track of care is my profession. That was the moment I realized the problem wasn’t effort — it was that our family’s most important information had no single place to live.

Every system covered a slice. Everything that fell between the slices fell on me.

So I built the thing I couldn’t find: an anchor — steady, holding — and flow — easy, moving with your family instead of against it. A calm place to set things down.

— LindseyFounder, nurse & homeschooling parent
